title: A finite birational map to a nodal curve with connected fibres is an isomorphism
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $X$ and $Y$ be reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], pure of dimension one [def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $Y$ is nodal: every nonsmooth closed point [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms] has completed local ring [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] isomorphic as a $k$-algebra to $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be finite and surjective [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Suppose there is an open $U\subset Y$ meeting every irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] such that $f^{-1}(U)\to U$ is an isomorphism, and that every geometric fibre [def-weil-geometric-fibre] of $f$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then $f$ is an isomorphism. Neither $X$ nor $Y$ is required to be connected, separated or proper over $k$.
